note: Column 16 of docs/contracts/documentation-parity-ledger.md. A route appears here ONLY if it was opened in a browser and looked at. Everything else in that ledger is measured by e2e/ledger-evidence.spec.ts across all 105 routes — this file is the part that cannot be measured, and it is deliberately shorter than 105. A route missing from it reads as not-yet-reviewed rather than as passing, which is the whole reason the column exists.
howToRead: Each entry names the viewports and themes actually opened, and what the review found. `found` is empty when the page was read and nothing was wrong; it is not a claim that nothing ever will be.
coverage: 107 of 107 routes opened in a browser. 24 were reviewed in the first-preview sweep at several widths and both themes; the remaining 83 (plus reveal-bloom and media-scrim, new this round) were opened at 1440 light on 2026-09-12 against the production build, and 25 of those also at 375 dark — four by screenshot, twenty-one by measuring document and stage overflow. `found` records what was wrong and what was done; an empty `found` means the page was read and nothing was wrong. Every other column in the documentation ledger is measured by e2e/ledger-evidence.spec.ts.

found: Opening specimen was a single `<Button>Open Pack</Button>` — one arbitrary state. Replaced with all seven variants side by side; Variants and Sizes keep their own sections below.
Opened with a `snippet` and no live preview at all. Now a real react-hook-form + Zod specimen in a companion client file; submitting empty shows both field errors.
`CommandDialog` dropped its children into `DialogContent` with no `Command` root — the page returned "This page couldn't load" in a production build.
The search field painted no focus ring: `InputGroup` keys its ring off `data-slot=input-group-control` and cmdk needs `command-input` there. Measured broken: five transparent shadows.
The palette specimen used `defaultOpen`, which made the whole page inert. Now opened by a button, on ⌘J so it does not steal the shell's ⌘K.
`defaultOpen` on a modal: body computed `pointer-events: none`, article unscrollable. `modal={false}` does not help — `DialogContent` always renders a full-viewport overlay. Reverted to a trigger.
Same as dialog, and `AlertDialog` cannot be non-modal at all — Radix hard-sets `modal: true` after the prop spread. Reverted to a trigger.
`defaultOpen modal={false}` still computed `pointer-events: none` on the body. vaul's source suggests otherwise; the browser settled it. Reverted to a trigger.

Prose inside the specimen wrapped to about one word per line. `Meta` split its columns on a viewport breakpoint while sitting in a 20rem column, leaving 56px for the description. Fixed with a container query; cells now measure 238px.

The capability did not exist: the contract named it and the architecture doc promised utilities that nothing implemented. Seven `*-safe` utilities shipped, page rewritten, all seven verified emitted and resolving.
The specimen's own first draft put `p-safe` and `p-4` on one element; both write the same longhands, so the later rule won and it measured 0px while its caption claimed otherwise.

The hero description printed literal backticks — `meta.description` is one string read by four things and only the hero can render markup. Seven descriptions were affected; split into lib/ds/docs/description.ts.

The chart's lines look absent in a Browser-pane screenshot. Measured: two recharts paths with real `d`, token strokes and opacity 1, frozen mid draw-on animation because the pane does not composite. Not a page defect.
Its description pointed at `/design-system/components/base/charts`, a route deleted in this change. Rewritten to name the two components it actually documents.

Listed the Documentation group as if it were components — Introduction, Installation and Changelog rendered as cards beside Button — and its blurb still described three families and a Site family removed months ago. Rewritten as four catalog-derived family sections; 105 cards, no authored list.
The entrance timelines had already played by the time the page settled, so the specimen was a still grid. It now replays through a Tabs remount — four timelines, side by side, on demand.

Writing its Responsive section surfaced a real component defect: the previous/next chevrons carry a `data-icon="inline-start"`/`"inline-end"` marker that no CSS rule mirrors, so the arrows point the wrong way under RTL. The page records it; the component still needs fixing.
Preview stage measured 640px with the pagination centred; nine sections after it closed by default, opening on click and on their own hash.
Opened with one class on one button. Now the four press utilities side by side with their scale values, so the difference between them is the thing on screen.

Its meta description promised a focus ring, keyboard operation and a 44px target that the CSS never supplied — that was Flutter's `Press` widget's surface written onto a web capability that is one transform.
Its fill uses a `translateX` calc with no RTL variant, so the bar fills from the wrong edge in a mirrored layout. Recorded on the page; queued as a component fix.
First capture caught the sliding pill mid-entrance (washed); second capture correct.
